ImageDescription.value:
“The Strip” (part of the Las Vegas Boulevard) in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA
The Las Vegas Strip is the most famous section of Las Vegas Boulevard in Las Vegas. It stretches for around 6.8 kilometers south of downtown and is world-famous for its spectacular hotels, casinos, and neon signs.
Its development began in the 1940s with the construction of large resort hotels such as the Flamingo Las Vegas. In the following decades, ever larger themed hotels were built, including the Bellagio with its famous water features and the Roman-style Caesars Palace. The Strip stands for entertainment in XXL format: casinos, shows, concerts, luxury shopping, and elaborate architecture characterize the scene. Many buildings feature international motifs – from Egyptian pyramids to the Eiffel Tower.
Today, the Las Vegas Strip is one of the most visited tourist destinations in the USA and a symbol of glamour, gambling and night-time lights in the Nevada desert.

ImageDescription.value:
Intake towers of the Hoover Dam on the side of Nevada, Nevada/Arizona, USA
The Hoover Dam is a monumental dam on the Colorado River between the states of Nevada and Arizona. It was built between 1931 and 1936 during the Great Depression and was one of the largest construction projects of its time. Thousands of workers were involved; the construction was considered a technical masterpiece.
The dam is named after President Herbert Hoover, who promoted the project politically. The enormous arch dam is around 221 meters high and consists of millions of cubic meters of concrete. It dams the Colorado River to form Lake Mead, one of the largest reservoirs in the USA.
The aim of the project was flood control, irrigation, and power generation for the southwestern United States. To this day, the hydroelectric power plant supplies energy to millions of people. The Hoover Dam is considered a symbol of American engineering and economic prosperity.
